title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
slides: What if your AI is already compromised?
Microsoft CEO warns: assume all AI models are compromised.
Security experts debate what 'compromised' really means.
Audit your AI tools for hidden backdoors now.
thread_text:
1. Your AI might be compromised

Microsoft's CEO says you should assume every AI model you use has already been tampered with. Not a possibility — a baseline.

2. The assumption we ignore

Most teams treat model poisoning as a rare edge case. The warning flips that: treat every deployed model as potentially hostile until proven otherwise.

3. What 'compromised' actually means

Security researchers can't agree. It could be training data injection, weight manipulation, or a hidden trigger — each demands a different defense.

4. The backdoor you can't see

A compromised model behaves normally 99% of the time. That 1% is what attackers wait for — and standard testing won't catch it.

5. Audit before you trust

Run a red-team prompt on your main AI tool this week. If it fails, you've found your first real priority.

Assume every AI model you use has already been tampered with. That's Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's baseline, not a worst-case scenario. 🚨
